led-savings-calculator.assumptionNote: CO2 savings use a rough grid average of 0.4 kg per kWh; your country's grid may differ. Savings assume bulbs run the same hours before and after the upgrade.
benefits: A typical 10-bulb home saves over $100 a year with a one-time bulb swap.
LEDs last 15,000 to 25,000 hours versus about 1,000 for incandescents - fewer ladder trips.
Less wasted heat: LEDs stay cool, which also cuts summer cooling load slightly.
Lower electricity use means a smaller carbon footprint from your lighting.
The math pays for the bulbs in months, then keeps paying you every year.

faqs.a: An LED uses roughly 80 to 90 percent less power for the same brightness. A 60 W incandescent is replaced by a 9 W LED, an 100 W by a 15 W LED. Same light, one-tenth of the energy.
faqs.q: How much less power does an LED use?

faqs.a: The wattage is printed on the old bulb, often near the base. Common incandescent sizes: 40, 60, 75, and 100 W. If you are unsure, 60 W is a safe guess for a standard room bulb.
faqs.q: How do I find my old bulb's wattage?

faqs.a: Wattage measures power use; lumens measure brightness. Match lumens when buying: an 800-lumen LED gives about the same light as a 60 W incandescent. The bulb box shows both.
faqs.q: What is the difference between watts and lumens?

faqs.a: Often not, at typical electricity prices. LEDs cost more per bulb but pay back in months through energy savings, then save money for their whole 15,000-plus-hour life.
Check your electricity bill or your utility's website. US homes average around $0.15 to $0.20 per kWh, India around 6 to 10 rupees per kWh. Enter your own rate for an accurate result.
faqs.q: What electricity rate should I use?

faqs.a: Multiply your annual savings by 5, 10, or 15 years. Ten 60 W to 9 W bulbs at 5 hours a day and $0.15 per kWh save about $140 a year - over $2,000 across 15 years.

led-savings-calculator.formula:
Yearly kWh saved = (Old watts - New watts) / 1000 x Bulbs x Hours per day x 365
Yearly money saved = kWh saved x Cost per kWh
Percent saved = (Old watts - New watts) / Old watts x 100

Example: (60 - 9) / 1000 x 10 x 5 x 365 = 930.75 kWh per year.
howTo: Enter how many bulbs you are replacing.
Enter the wattage of an old bulb and the wattage of the new LED.
Enter hours per day the lights are on, and your electricity cost per kWh.
Read your yearly kWh savings, money savings, and CO2 reduction.
keyFacts: A 60 W incandescent replaced by a 9 W LED saves 85% of the lighting energy.
Lighting is about 10 to 15% of a typical home's electricity use.
LEDs last 15,000 to 25,000 hours. Incandescents last about 1,000 hours.
CFLs sit in the middle: a 14 W CFL replaces a 60 W bulb but contains mercury.
Match lumens, not watts: 800 lumens is roughly a 60 W incandescent's brightness.
LEDs produce very little heat, so they do not warm your rooms like old bulbs.
Dimmable LEDs need a compatible dimmer switch. Old dimmers often flicker with LEDs.
Payback: an LED usually pays for itself in a few months of normal use.

led-savings-calculator.quickAnswer: Switching 10 bulbs from 60 W to 9 W LEDs, used 5 hours a day at $0.15 per kWh, saves about 931 kWh and $139.61 per year - an 85% cut in lighting energy. Enter your own numbers above for your exact savings.
led-savings-calculator.tagline: See exactly how much money, energy, and CO2 you save by switching to LED bulbs.
led-savings-calculator.workedExample:
10 bulbs, 60 W to 9 W, 5 hours per day, $0.15 per kWh.
1. Watts saved per bulb: 60 - 9 = 51 W. Total: 510 W = 0.51 kW.
2. Hours per year: 5 x 365 = 1825.
3. kWh saved: 0.51 x 1825 = 930.75 kWh per year.
4. Money saved: 930.75 x 0.15 = $139.61 per year.
5. Percent saved: 51 / 60 = 85%. CO2 avoided: 930.75 x 0.4 = 372.3 kg per year.
